newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sugar producers could get refund.
newsitem.headline: EU sugar producers could get refund.

text.p: The European Union's sugar management committee will consider on Wednesday whether refunds should be made to producers under the production levy system, an EU official said on Monday.
"If the result of the committee's financial review of the past few weeks is that revenue needed is more than the outlay there could be a question of a refund," the official said.
The committee has been reviewing production and export costs and would have to implement a special regulation for reimbursement, the official explained.
A vote may be taken if there are no new revisions of the figures.
The committee will also continue to review exports to ensure that GATT (General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade) limits are being met, the official said.
"This is an ongoing review and no conclusion is expected," he said.
The committee will further discuss setting an annual guideline for the monthly export refund for products which have a sugar content.
"The refund for these non-Annex II products is set monthly but it is felt that it would be useful to have a guideline for the year showing how the figures are decided each month," the official said.
The committee will also decide monthly export tenders and molasses import duties.
